articleTitle: Nonintrusive partial discharge measurements on high voltage switchgear
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: Partial discharges in high voltage metal-clad switchgear can result in catastrophic failure of the individual plant and in some cases of the substation. There has been a need for detection and location of the damaging discharges without the plant or substation being taken out of service. The conventional partial discharge detection technique requires direct connection to the high voltage busbars and therefore is limited in application. The EA Technology Partial Discharge Locator and Partial Discharge Monitor are designed to fulfil this important requirement. These instruments are complemented by ultrasonic detection to provide a comprehensive service to both Regional Electricity Companies and industry. The Partial Discharge Locator and Partial Discharge Monitor both use the Transient Earth Voltage (TEV) measurement technique. The Partial Discharge Locator is a portable instrument used to survey switchrooms taking approximately an hour to survey a ten panel switchboard. The Partial Discharge Monitor is installed for a week monitoring a switchboard and provides a means of detecting intermittent partial discharge activity which may be missed by a survey with the Partial Discharge Locator.

articleTitle: Condition assessment of circuit breakers using a trip coil profiling approach
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: This paper highlights the benefits of the technique known as coil profiling. The experience gained through extensive field trials are discussed, and the future strategy for the condition assessment of circuit breakers within Northern Ireland Electricity plc (NIE) is outlined. Coil profiling has provided a method which not only assists in the pin pointing of defects after failure, but can provide diagnostic information highlighting areas of potential failure which would otherwise have gone undetected. It is a technique which has proved both reliable and accurate and lends itself to a variety of maintenance strategies. There are many devices on the market which can record coil current profiles. This paper does not attempt to recommend a specific product, as the merits of each is dependant upon the strategy employed.

articleTitle: Circuit breaker condition assessment by vibration and trip coil analysis
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: Some method of assessing a circuit breaker's condition or readiness to trip is required. This must be a quick, noninvasive test which enables the operator to know how the breaker would operate from 'cold'. This method of screening plant would enable maintenance money and resources to be targeted in a much more effective manner. This paper introduces the Profile System, which has been developed by Kelman Ltd. in order to address these issues. This instrument provides a quick and easy method of assessing the condition of circuit breakers by simply performing an open and close operation. The two main techniques used by this instrument to assess circuit breaker condition are trip coil profiling and vibration monitoring. These methods are outlined.

articleTitle: The Hydran/sup (R/)-a system for the detection and monitoring of failure conditions in power transformers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: The author discusses early detection of transformer faults using dissolved gas analysis. The author describes Hydran technology used in dissolved gas analysis, and in particular the Hydran 201R on-line gas in oil monitor, the Hydran 201R Model i (microprocessor controlled device) and the Hydran 103B portable battery powered device.

articleTitle: Advances in circuit breaker testing and condition monitoring
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: Hathaway Systems Limited, located in Belfast, Northern Ireland is a subsidiary of the Hathaway Corporation of Denver, Colorado. Hathaway Systems Limited has designed and produced diagnostic systems used specifically for testing transmission and distribution circuit breakers for ten years. These systems have been used by engineers throughout the world to provide the information required to ensure the integrity of a breaker before, during and after routine maintenance. This paper discusses various testing techniques for high voltage circuit breakers and motorised isolators and introduces some new approaches in this field.

articleTitle: Transformer condition assessment with the Tettex recovery voltage method
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: All oil-paper transformers contain some water in their solid insulation. The Tettex Recovery Voltage Meter (RVM) is a method for determining the moisture content in the paper so that the effects on dielectric integrity, loading capability and residual life expectancy can be estimated. The author discusses the problems of moisture in paper insulation, the polarisation effects and polarisation spectrum measurement using the Tettex RVM. Practical applications of the method are outlined and it is compared with other methods.

articleTitle: A design for a portable monitor to measure the HF content of SF/sub 6/
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: The paper describes a design for a portable monitor to determine the hydrogen fluoride content of sulphur hexafluoride over the range 0-100 ppm by volume. The monitor is intended for use by nontechnical staff, operates from rechargeable batteries, does not contain any consumable chemical solutions, and is easily maintained.

articleTitle: Enhancing network management with modern protection relays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: Management of electrical power networks requires an intimate knowledge of the performance of their many constituent items of plant. Performance of the network can only be assured if all of the plant items are able to perform in accordance with their design criteria. Outages to carry out preventative maintenance are becoming more difficult to obtain, and down sizing has, in many cases, reduced the availability of skilled staff to carry out work to maintain adequate performance. New techniques are now available based on the employment of communicating relays and the regular gathering of performance data which provides alternatives to the traditional way of doing things. The implications from the use of such numerical devices must be thoroughly understood in order to take advantage of their full capabilities. The author discusses network management using performance measurement, using protection relays for performance measurement, remote system analysis, and future developments.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: Economic pressure means utilities are holding back on investment in new equipment and reducing manpower expenses. Transformers are simply not being replaced as often as they were in the past. Transformers are being loaded more heavily, without adding new transformers. The key method to offset reduced maintenance personnel is to change from a calendar-based "scheduled" maintenance to a "predictive" maintenance philosophy, which focuses maintenance resources when and where the equipment "requires". On-line diagnostic systems, which continuously monitor critical parameters for symptoms indicating impending problems, provide the tools to do this. The QualiTROL SENTRY system provides an economical method to monitor transformers more closely, allowing utilities to analyze transformer behavior without costly travel to the site, predict potential problems, diagnose problems remotely, and plan resources to deal with problem situations. Utilities can concentrate their limited manpower on the equipment that is in need of attention. The system is easily retrofitted to existing transformers using existing sensor access points. The SENTRY provides a base platform with the features to do all the necessary monitoring to meet today and tomorrow's requirements. It provides: on-line continuous monitoring, automatic alarm notification, remote access to present and historical data, local displays, controls and alarms, outputs for SCADA and future higher level systems, and the ability to have the information at any PC, wherever and by whomever it is needed.

articleTitle: INSITE/sup (R/) continuous monitoring system-information not data
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Monitors and Condition Assessment Equipment (Digest No. 1996/186)
abstract: This paper discusses INSITE, the Doble Engineering Company's on-line continuous diagnostic monitoring system. It also reviews the INSITE platform and gives some examples of how the rule based expert system performs analysis. The INSITE substation apparatus monitoring system consists of sensors, data acquisition units, ModBus Plus/sup TM/ local area network communications, the INSITE controller (substation computer), PC-based user interface program, expert system analysis programme and databases. INSITE provides continuous condition monitoring and diagnostics of substation apparatus. It sends prioritised maintenance ALERTs indicating the severity and probable cause of incipient problems.
